# Question

This table shows the ages of the girls and boys in a club.

| Age | Number of Girls | Number of Boys |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8 | 4 | 6 |
| 9 | 8 | 4 |
| 10 | 6 | 10 |

Use the information in the table to complete the graph for ages 9 and 10.

[Image: Double bar graph]

Figure, described in words:
An incomplete double bar graph. The vertical axis is labeled "Number" with tick marks and horizontal grid lines at 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10. The horizontal axis is labeled "Age" with positions for 8, 9, and 10. A legend in the upper right shows a dark grey shaded square labeled "Girls" and an unshaded (white) square labeled "Boys". For age 8, two bars are plotted: a grey shaded bar of height 4 (Girls) followed by an adjacent white unshaded bar of height 6 (Boys). For ages 9 and 10, no bars are drawn.

# Scoring guide of the question (2 points)

- Correct Response (2 points):
  - All 4 bars correct for height, placement, and shading.
  - All 4 bars of correct height; either bars misplaced or bars shaded incorrectly in no more than one set (i.e., for age 9 or age 10).
- Partially Correct (1 point):
  - Placement, shading, and height all correct for one, two, or three bars. (At least one bar completely correct).
  - All 4 bars of correct height, but two or more errors involving placement or shading.
- Incorrect Response (0 points):
  - Work is shown, but no bars are drawn. For example: only numbers are shown on the graph.
  - Other incorrect.

Complete the graph for age 9 and age 10 as follows. For age 9: draw a grey shaded bar (Girls) up to 8 on the Number axis, and directly beside it draw an unshaded white bar (Boys) up to 4. For age 10: draw a grey shaded bar (Girls) up to 6 on the Number axis, and directly beside it draw an unshaded white bar (Boys) up to 10. The bars for each age should be side by side, with the grey Girls bar on the left and the white Boys bar on the right, matching the age 8 pair already drawn.
